standard_prerequisites.name: A ring map that is flat at a prime is faithfully flat after localizing at that prime, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the local ring map from the base point to the source point faithfully flat, which is what allows the kernel computation to be tested after tensoring.

standard_prerequisites.name: The stalk of a pullback module is the tensor product of the stalk with the local ring, cited from the sheaves chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the stalk at the point of the pulled back sheaf with the tensor product used in the kernel computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of flatness by the vanishing of the kernel of the tensor product with an injection of modules, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the displayed equality of kernels into the equivalence of flatness statements asserted by the lemma.

core_obligations: Set up the local situation: let s be the image of y and consider the chain of local ring maps from the local ring of the base at s to the local ring of the source at x; by the flatness hypothesis the second map is faithfully flat (proof lines 5113-5117).

Identify the pulled back stalk: write N for the stalk of the given sheaf at y and observe that the stalk at x of its pullback is the tensor product of N with the local ring of the source at x (proof lines 5118-5121).

Compute kernels: for an injection of modules over the base local ring, faithful flatness shows that the kernel of the tensor product with N becomes, after further tensoring with the source local ring, the kernel of the tensor product with the pulled back stalk; hence the equivalence of flatness statements follows from the kernel characterization of flatness (proof lines 5122-5142).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a chain of local rings with the second map faithfully flat (proof lines 5113-5117).
Transport the kernel criterion for flatness across those localizations through the displayed identity of kernels (proof lines 5118-5142).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a morphism h flat at a point x, flatness over the base of a sheaf at the image point is equivalent to flatness over the base of its pullback at x, with the two corollaries for a surjective flat h (statement lines 5097-5111). The counted proof is a direct local computation: it passes to the chain of local rings, uses the flatness hypothesis to get faithful flatness of the map to the source local ring, identifies the stalk of the pullback as a tensor product, and displays the identity of kernels that reduces the equivalence to the kernel characterization of flatness (proof lines 5113-5142). It is H2: the author notes that an algebra lemma would give the result, but the direct proof is carried out in the counted span.
